method: Valgrind/taintgrind DBI; 83 stdin bytes marked via TNT_TAINT client request, VEX-level bit taint propagated, taint log parsed for `Store` ops whose L:<addr> lies in canary_after
notes: taintgrind logged 20 tainted-value stores in nft_byteorder_eval, all stride-4 at 0x4bbbc0..0x4bbc0c (in-bounds within the 80-byte regs file). The verbatim trigger uses sreg=dreg=0 (IN-PLACE byteswap): the OOB iterations (i>=20) read the untainted canary constants and write them back byte-swapped, so their stored VALUE is not attacker-derived and taintgrind (precise VEX data-flow) does not taint them -- 0 tainted stores into canary_after [0x4bbc10,0x4bbd10). taintgrind DID see attacker influence on the loop trip count (`i < len/2` is a tainted IfGoto), a control dependence, not a tainted sink value/address. Note taintgrind is taint-only: it does not log the untainted OOB writes themselves (the canary IS corrupted, visible in the harness AFTER dump), unlike a mem-write hook. backend=docker

extra.harness_addr_note: layout recovered from taintgrind_tool/harness_tg.bin; canary_after = 0x4bbc10 (differs from the plain harness because the TNT_TAINT client-request calls shift symbol addresses)
